column1: # fanout.sh's jobs at 10M (msmarco-10000k): name, engine, shape, timeout in
# hours, and the job's own settings. Run with one pass and the bigger-disk
# nodes, e.g.
#   SHARDED_SIZE=m3-4vcpu-32gb ONE_SIZE=m3-8vcpu-64gb PASSES=1 LOAD_HOURS=16 \
#   COPY_JOBS=3 BUDGET=75 COLLECTION=msmarco-10000k fanout.sh run fanout-jobs-10m.tsv
# The timeouts are the 1M run's step times scaled to 10M (loads x11, the
# kinds that scan x10) with a third more, and bound the budget's worst case.
# Qdrant's load is the longest (its 1M index took 69 minutes), then
# Strata's two jobs, so that the comparison's own engine is sure to run;
# their 5 hours allow a build of about 2 hours (500K segments compacted to
# 2M ones, timed on the cloud container at 500K and 1M).
# Redis keeps everything in memory (8.2 GB at 1M), so it gets a 128 GB node
# with the same CPU limit as every one-node engine.
# Jobs start in this order as the budget allows: of the rest, Elasticsearch
# and OpenSearch (the engines closest to Strata at 1M) first, and Redis, on
# the costliest node, near the end. Milvus and Typesense ran out of memory at
# 52Gi (Typesense at 7.2M documents, Milvus building its index), so they run
# again on Redis's 128 GB node with the same CPU limit; ParadeDB, whose
# pgvector index builds like Postgres's (about 7 h at 10M), gets its 9 hours.
qdrant     qdrant     one      18
strata     strata     sharded  5
strata-b   strata     sharded  5
postgres   postgres   one      9
meili      meili      one      9
manticore  manticore  one      8
vespa      vespa      sharded  8
es         es         sharded  5
os         os         sharded  5
solr       solr       sharded  7
weaviate   weaviate   one      6
milvus     milvus     one      5   ONE_SIZE=m-16vcpu-128gb,ONE_MEM=110Gi
paradedb   paradedb   one      9
redis      redis      one      7   ONE_SIZE=m-16vcpu-128gb,ONE_MEM=110Gi,REDIS_MAXMEM=100000mb
typesense  typesense  one      8   ONE_SIZE=m-16vcpu-128gb,ONE_MEM=110Gi
